title: Down strokes and Dixieland bass and drum rhythm
summary: The down stroke is rhythm; the Dixieland bass and bass drum play first and third until the hot last chorus.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: To get back to your rhythm guitar, one of those are our banjo. There was a banjo player who came over here from England last year. Nice enough guy and knew the instruments fairly well. But he was always going plenka, plenka, plenka, plenka back and forth always a double stroke. Yes, yes. Well, usually do you just hit thumb the down stroke? Of course you have that more different style in your guitar. Yeah. That bass.
The down stroke, that down stroke is rhythm.
But you don't try to always snap back?

No, no, no. Because many of the double strokes. Now and then you'll hit a double stroke. For instance we'll say on, the way we used to use, used to add lead, even on the rhythm instrument, was on the last course what we call the hot chorus. All the instruments play as they should. The rhythm, play rhythm straight up. Now on the hot chorus everybody gets cut loose on that last chorus you see. Everybody's at liberty. The bass player, now you see like these bass players all night long, four beats to the bass, boom boom boom boom boom boom boom boom. That's not bass for the Dixieland. Solid. One, two, one, two, one, two. When it's not in. Do do do do do do do do do do do. Do do do do do. Do do do do. Do do do. Do do do. Do do do. Do do. Do do. One. That's bass.

That's bass for the dance orchestra. Now in the last chorus, everybody gets a window, you see. Then you get . You see everybody's at liberty in that last chorus, you're getting hot. But throughout the number, up until that last chorus, bass player is supposed to play first and third. Now the same with the drummer. Hell, four beats on the bass drum, man. That's all right for that last chorus. The bass drum is supposed to play the same as the bass. One, two, one, two, one, two. Whatever you do with the sticks on the snare drum, that bass is supposed to be . Now in that last chorus you want to get hot, that's the hot chorus. But you can't tell the youngsters that nowadays. You tell the bass player, play one, two, man. He says, man, some people come up here and they think I can't play no bass. That's their attitude, you see. Drummers likewise. And they all want to be Dixieland players. I mean they're not playing Dixieland.
